A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the thrombolytics, especially urokinase, have no adverse effects on platelets in vitro and in vivo, but the solution of PRP clot, which is formed after thrombolysis and contains thrombolytic products, has the potential to enhance platelet aggregation and thrombosis.
thrombolytic treatment in patients with acute myocardial infarction may increase the incidence of thrombotic events by enhancing platelet response to thrombin and ADP.
thrombolytic drugs may be safe for the platelet function in vivo, but LSPC may be a potent activator of platelets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LSPC may be a useful tool for studying the effects of thrombolytics on platelets in vivo.
thrombolytic treatment of patients with ischemic stroke may be associated with an increased risk of intracerebral hemorrhage due to the effects of the thrombolytics on the blood platelet.
the thrombolysis process itself can be a source of platelet activators and can contribute to thrombosis.
